sections.title: Abstract
sections.formatNote: Structured, no more than 180 words including its headings: Objectives (begins with "To"), Methods, Results, Conclusions, and Public Health Implications. No Background heading. State the date(s) and location(s) of the data.
sections.boilerplate:
Objectives. 
Methods. 
Results. 
Conclusions. 
Public Health Implications.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.formatNote: Paragraphs; the question the study answers and why it matters for public health.

sections.title: Methods
sections.formatNote: Paragraphs with subheadings as needed: data source(s) with dates and locations, design, measures, analysis. Name the IRB approval here, without the institution's name in the blinded manuscript.

sections.title: Results
sections.formatNote: Paragraphs; one decimal place for proportions and effect measures; exponentiated estimates with 95% CIs rather than parameter estimates; actual P values rounded to 2 decimals, never "NS".

sections.title: Discussion
sections.formatNote: Paragraphs: principal findings, context with prior work, limitations, and what follows for practice, policy and research.

sections.title: Public Health Implications
sections.formatNote: A short closing section of its own.
sections.note: Named explicitly in this journal's instructions — practice, policy and research.
sections.boilerplate: What these findings mean for public health practice, policy and research.

sections.title: Submission Questions
sections.note: The questions Editorial Manager asks at submission, answered here so they travel with the manuscript and can be pasted in.

questions.prompt: What is the public health importance of the paper?
Provide a description of what the paper adds to current knowledge base, particularly with respect to material previously published in AJPH, and if systematic reviews exist on the topic.
Provide one sentence summarizing the main message(s) of the paper. This is important as it may be used on social media (e.g., AJPH Twitter, etc) to highlight the findings of the paper.
